## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Ekadussadāyakattheraapadāna* is a verse narrative found in the Therāpadāna of the Pali Canon's Khuddaka Nikāya, designated as Tha Ap 424 [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts the past merit and spiritual career of the elder Ekadussadāyaka. SuttaCentral notes translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].

Computational analysis by DharmaNexus records extensive text reuse across the Pali canon and commentarial literature, comprising 184 matches across 50 Pali works [DharmaNexus]. Strikingly, almost the entire initial narrative (§0.2–19.1) is virtually identical to another homonymous text in the collection, the *Ekadussadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 336), with a 0.98 similarity score [DharmaNexus]. Verses are also preserved in the commentary to the Theragāthā (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, its stock verses (§18.1–23.1) are widely shared with neighboring poems such as the *Ekāsanadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 425), *Yāgudāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 420), and *Upaḍḍhadussadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 497) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated alignments, DharmaNexus reports correspondences with Sanskrit texts including the *Kaṭhināvadāna* and the *Tathāgatabimbakārāpaṇasūtra*, as well as low-scoring parallels in the Tibetan translation of the *Suhṛllekha* [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
